item.title: FB post to blow up Puri Srimandir: Odisha Police arrest accused
item.description: Puri: A day after a threatening social media post claiming a bomb attack on Shree Jagannath Temple in Puri sent shockwaves across the pilgrimage town, Odisha Police swung into immediate action and have arrested a youth in this connection. item.title: Beheaded Body of Elderly Man Found in Jajpur Village, Murder Suspected
item.description: Jajpur: The beheaded body of an elderly man was found lying on the roadside at Matigadia village under Sukinda Police Station limits in Odisha's Jajpur district on Thursday morning. The deceased has been identified as Dasarath Behera, a resident of the same village. Circumstances Point to Murder The body was spotted around 100 metres away from his house. item.title: President to Visit Odisha in First Week of February, Attend FM University Convocation
item.description: Bhubaneswar: President Droupadi Murmu is scheduled to visit Odisha in the first week of February and take part in several official and cultural programmes. According to reports, the President will arrive in Odisha on February 2 for a five-day visit. She will reach Bhubaneswar on the same day and stay overnight in the state capital. item.description: Mumbai: Bollywood actor Varun Dhawan has opened up about how his upcoming film Border 2 proved to be a deeply transformative experience for him, both professionally and personally. item.title: Climbdown in Greenland tensions to boost market sentiments, help rupee recover
item.description: New Delhi: The overnight signs of a climbdown in Greenland-related tensions will provide relief to market sentiments and rupee volatility is likely to persist in the near term but depreciation is expected to be more gradual than the recent sharp moves, a report showed on Thursday. Market sentiment improves as rupee gains 15 paise against dollar The rupee rebounded from its all-time low levels to gain 15 paise at 91.50 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday. item.title: Process begins for Odisha Rajya Sabha polls as 4 MPs set to retire on April 2
item.description: Bhubaneswar: The process for the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Odisha has begun with the Election Commission of India writing to the Chief Electoral Officer of Odisha to initiate preparations. Four Rajya Sabha members from Odisha are scheduled to retire on April 2, creating vacancies that will be filled through the election process. item.title: Sajjan Kumar acquitted in 1984 riots cases
item.description: New Delhi: A Delhi court on Thursday acquitted former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar in connection with the alleged killings of two Sikhs, Sohan Singh and his son-in-law Avtar Singh, in Delhi's Janakpuri, and another incident in Vikaspuri where one Gurcharan Singh was allegedly set ablaze, during the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. item.title: Odisha: High Court allows rape survivor to terminate pregnancy, orders fetal DNA Test
item.description: Cuttack: In a landmark ruling, the Orissa High Court has permitted a rape survivor to undergo medical termination of pregnancy and directed that a DNA test of the fetus be conducted and produced before the court as evidentiary material. The survivor had approached the High Court seeking permission for abortion as well as DNA examination of the fetus. item.title: Paddy trader paraded with hands tied in Odisha’s Mayurbhanj; video goes viral
item.description: Udala: A video circulating on social media shows a paddy trader allegedly being forced to walk through village streets with his hands tied in Odisha’s Mayurbhanj district. The incident reportedly took place in Kainsari village under Udala police limits. item.title: Encounter breaks out between Maoists and security forces in Saranda Forest of Jharkhand
item.description: Chaibasa (Jharkhand): A fierce encounter has been going on since Thursday morning between security forces and Maoists in the Saranda forest region of Jharkhand’s West Singhbhum district. While reports suggest that several Maoists have been killed, official confirmation on the exact number of casualties is still awaited.
